text: Proseware renewal is coming up fast. Our CloudOps contract (managed Azure for their policy and claims platforms) ends 31 Mar, current ACV $410k. Duncan Kilbride (Head of Cloud & Infrastructure) is happy with us, but Bianca Moretti in vendor mgmt says anything over $250k goes to competitive review this year.

Woodgrove Bank Jan service desk numbers: 18,400 tickets, FCR 68%, CSAT 4.1. Contract is $1.15M ACV for 2,300 users and renews 30 Jun. Teodora Constantin (Head of IT Ops) told me she wants FCR above 72% before we even start renewal talks.

Proseware observability pilot agreed w/ Duncan. 6 weeks, $18k fixed fee, credited back if they buy the full service. 20 claims platform services in scope, kickoff planned Mon 9 Feb. Raf Quintero (cloud platform mgr) is their lead. Success criteria: alert noise down 50%, MTTR down 30% from the 47 min baseline.

Lucerne Publishing royalties migration update from Nkechi Obi (Royalties & Contracts Mgr): data mapping about 70% done, cutover still planned for 6 Apr. Spring royalty statements to ~4,800 authors have to go out of the new system by 30 Apr, zero slack on that date.

Woodgrove Win11 migration: Pavel Hrabal (EUC lead) says the Jan pilot on 120 devices went fine, only 3 rollbacks. Main rollout begins Mon 16 Feb with the North region branches (410 devices), then Central from 9 Mar. 1,850 devices in total, fixed price $640k.

Lucerne: Felix Brandauer (Head of Digital) wants a proof of concept for AI metadata tagging on their backlist, 24k titles. $15k is the most he can sign without going to Wilhelmina Strathearn, their CFO. He wants a proposal by Fri 13 Feb.

prep me for Thursday 11am with Ottilie Marchbank, Proseware's CFO. She joined in Sept and I've only met her once. Agenda is the CloudOps renewal ($410k ACV, ends 31 Mar) and vendor mgmt's competitive review. What will she care about and what should I ask her?

Draft the agenda for the Woodgrove QBR on Tue 10 Feb, 10-12 at their HQ. Harriet Wanjiru (CIO), Teodora and Pavel attending. Items: Jan service desk stats (FCR 68%, CSAT 4.1), FCR improvement plan, Win11 readiness for the 16 Feb start, renewal timeline to 30 Jun. Keep it tight.

fyi Raf Quintero at Proseware wants everything operational in the shared slack channel #proseware-ops, he ignores email in his on-call weeks. Also their CISO Yusuf Demir has to approve the monitoring agent install before the pilot can start. Raf says he's thorough but slow.

Lucerne: Nkechi prefers calls after 2pm, mornings she's buried in author and agent queries. Also realised she's the only person there who really understands the old royalty rules (escalators, reserves against returns). Single point of failure for the migration.

Just off with Ottilie Marchbank. She wants a 2-yr option priced, wants to see pilot results before signing anything, and anything commercial has to be in her inbox the evening before - she reads email at 7am ahead of her 8:30 exec meeting. I floated a 5% uplift, she didnt love it.

Woodgrove: Josh Tremblay (third-party risk mgr) emailed. Their regulator wants a documented exit plan for every critical outsourced service, ours (service desk) is due 31 Mar. Plus a 120-question due diligence questionnaire, due 27 Feb.

Draft the proposal summary for Felix's metadata POC: 2,000 backlist titles as the sample, 4 weeks, we generate BISAC subject codes + keywords, accuracy target 85% against his editors' own tags. $14.5k fixed so he can sign it himself under his $15k limit.

draft the pilot kickoff post for #proseware-ops (Raf + team) for Mon 9 Feb: 20 claims services in scope, 6 weeks, targets alert noise -50% and MTTR -30% vs the 47 min baseline. Mention we still need Yusuf's sign-off on the agent install. Short, it's slack.

Lucerne: Linus Penhaligon (IT Mgr) told me Wilhelmina Strathearn sent back our last SOW unread because it was a PDF. She wants Word docs so she can track-change them. So every commercial doc for her goes in Word from now on.

Proseware pilot did NOT start today. Yusuf Demir hasn't approved the agent install, he wants our latest pen test summary first. Sent it at 11. Raf thinks Wed is realistic, so the pilot end date moves too.

prep me for tmrw's Woodgrove QBR. Harriet will push on FCR (68% vs the 72% Teodora wants). I also want to plant the MDR idea - Teodora let slip their SOC provider contract ends 31 Aug and Harriet is unhappy with their response times. Who cares about what in that room?

Woodgrove QBR done. Harriet happy with CSAT, not with FCR. We agreed to add 2 L2 engineers for 8 weeks at our cost to push knowledge articles. Harriet wants an MDR proposal by 13 Mar, budget around $300k/yr. Teodora: for any P1 she wants a phone call first, email after, never email only.

draft the QBR follow-up email to Harriet Wanjiru, cc Teodora: thanks for teh time, 2 extra L2 engineers for 8 weeks at our cost on knowledge articles, FCR target 72% by end of March, MDR proposal by 13 Mar, exit plan to Josh by 31 Mar.

Lucerne steerco: Linus says the AS/400 extract has 11,000 contract records with the territory fields missing. Nkechi reckons 3 weeks of manual cleanup and she's the only one who can do it. 6 Apr cutover now at risk.

Yusuf signed off first thing, so the Proseware observability pilot started on Wed 11 Feb, not the 9th. Agents going onto 14 of the 20 services today, the other 6 by Fri. Keeping the full 6 weeks means it now ends 25 Mar.

prep for my 2:30 with Nkechi on the contract data cleanup. 11k records missing territory, she estimates 3 weeks by hand, cutover 6 Apr at risk and statements due 30 Apr. What options can I put to her to speed it up without burning her out?

Nkechi call went well. We script a first pass using territory data from their rights database and she only reviews the exceptions. Should cut it to ~8 working days. Extra effort on our side ~12 days, so a $16.8k change request (12 x $1,400).

Bianca Moretti (Proseware vendor mgmt) sent a 40-question RFI style questionnaire for the CloudOps renewal, due 20 Feb. She also mentioned another MSP quoted 12% under our current price. Wouldn't say who.

Woodgrove: Josh wants our SOC 2 Type II report and latest BCP test evidence with the questionnaire. SOC 2 is from Oct so fine. Our last BCP test was June 2025, hes ok as long as the next one is booked before June.

Felix signed the metadata POC at $14.5k, starts Mon 23 Feb. He also said, very casually, that he's had a demo from a Shopify agency for the bookstore. Our retainer ($26k/month) renews 1 May. Need to watch this.
what do I still owe Proseware right now? want to clear it before the weekend

Harriet called: Augustin Valcourt, Woodgrove's CFO, wants the MDR to go through their investment committee. It meets the first Tuesday of each month, papers due the Thursday before. For the 3 Mar committee that means papers by 26 Feb, otherwise it's 7 Apr. Harriet wants 3 Mar. And nothing goes to Augustin direct from vendors, always via Harriet's office.

Draft my reply to Bianca's questionnaire email: we'll return all 40 answers by 20 Feb, ask for 30 min to walk her through the SLA section, and gently point out the 12% cheaper quote probably doesn't include 24x7 P1 cover. Polite, not defensive.
Woodgrove Win11 rollout started on Mon 16 Feb as planned, North region. 96 devices done on day one, 2 failures, both old Latitude 5400s with the BIOS issue. Pavel happy so far.

Draft the cover note for the change request to Wilhelmina Strathearn: $16.8k for the scripted cleanup of the 11k contract records, protects the 6 Apr cutover and the 30 Apr royalty statements. I'll paste it into the Word doc, she'll track-change it anyway.

Proseware pilot week 1: alert volume down 38% (from ~1,900 to ~1,180 a week), MTTR 47 to 39 min across 6 incidents. Raf pleased. He wants to add the document imaging service too, which is outside the agreed scope.

need an outline for the Woodgrove MDR paper for the investment committee (papers due 26 Feb). Budget ~$300k/yr, replaces their SOC contract ending 31 Aug, 2,300 users and 140 branches. Augustin Valcourt will read every word. What sections and in what order?
Wilhelmina approved the $16.8k CR, with tracked changes - she capped expenses at $500. She wants a cutover readiness report from us every week until go-live, RAG format, sent to her and Nkechi.

Big Proseware news: Duncan Kilbride is promoted to Deputy CIO from 1 Mar. Raf Quintero becomes acting Head of Cloud & Infrastructure and owns the technical sign-off on the renewal now. Duncan stays our exec sponsor.

Woodgrove Win11 week 1: 388 of 410 North devices done, 7 rollbacks. Problem: their teller app BranchOne crashes on 24H2 at 3 branches. Pavel has raised it with the vendor. Central wave on 9 Mar might slip.

Sent Bianca all 40 questionnaire answers this morning, on time. She now wants pricing on 3 options: 1-yr at current scope, 2-yr at current scope, and 2-yr including observability. Wants it before their exec mtg on 26 Feb.

Draft the first weekly cutover readiness report for Lucerne (to Wilhelmina + Nkechi), RAG: data cleanup amber (script running, 4,200 of 11,000 done), environments green, 6 Apr cutover amber, 30 Apr statements green. Short, they'll read it on their phones.
Lucerne metadata POC started today, 2,000 titles loaded. Felix's team will tag 200 by hand as the benchmark. Also heard Margot Delacroix joins as COO on 2 Mar and Felix will report to her.

Woodgrove MDR pricing done internally: $286k/yr for 2,300 users on a 3-yr term, plus $24k one-off onboarding. Harriet has seen the numbers and is fine. Josh's due diligence questionnaire is about 80% done, due Fri.

prep me for tmrw's internal pricing review on Proseware. Bianca's 3 options (1-yr, 2-yr, 2-yr + observability), current $410k, the 5% uplift I floated, Ottilie wanting 2-yr, the mystery MSP 12% cheaper. What's a sensible walk-away?

Proseware pricing review outcome: 1-yr at +5% = $430.5k. 2-yr at +3.5% = $424.4k/yr. 2-yr plus observability = $489.4k/yr (observability list is $65k). Floor is +2% on the 2-yr, only if they commit to observability.

draft the cover memo for Augustin Valcourt to go with the MDR paper, via Harriet's office: $286k/yr, 3-yr term, $24k onboarding, replaces the SOC contract ending 31 Aug with a 30-day overlap for transition. Goes to the 3 Mar investment committee. Formal, he's a numbers guy.

Bad news on Lucerne. Script cleaned 7,900 records but 3,100 need Nkechi's manual review, not the ~1,000 we hoped. She thinks 2 more weeks. 6 Apr cutover is off, proposing 20 Apr. Statements still due 30 Apr, so only 10 days of buffer.

draft the pricing email to Ottilie and Bianca with the 3 options from yesterday's review. Lead with the 2-yr + observability. Sending it tonight so it's in Ottilie's inbox for her 7am read before tomorrow's exec mtg.

Woodgrove service desk phones were down 8:10 to 8:57 this morning. Carrier SIP trunk failed and failover to the backup trunk didn't kick in. Called Teodora at 8:20 like she wants, she was not happy. Getting the numbers together now.
Outage email sent to Teodora at 9:40: 47 min, 312 abandoned calls. She wants a full RCA by Mon noon and asked straight out about service credits.

weekly cutover report #2 for Wilhelmina and Nkechi pls. Data cleanup red (7,900 done, 3,100 need manual review), cutover proposed to move 6 Apr -> 20 Apr pending Wilhelmina's ok, statements 30 Apr amber, environments green.
Woodgrove MDR paper went to the investment committee today, on deadline. Harriet attached her own note backing it, which helps. Committee sits Tue 3 Mar.

Draft the RCA summary for Teodora Constantin on yesterday's phone outage: 47 min (8:10-8:57), 312 abandoned calls, root cause carrier SIP trunk failover misconfigured after their maintenance on 21 Feb. Fixes: weekly failover test, second carrier by 31 Mar. Offer the 5% service credit on the Feb desk fee (~$4.8k).

Proseware pilot week 2: alert noise down 55% vs baseline, MTTR 35 min. Noise target hit, MTTR not there yet (-26%). Raf wants the numbers posted in #proseware-ops every Monday morning from now on. Told him document imaging waits for the full rollout.

Woodgrove changes: Pavel Hrabal moved to their digital channels team as of today, Teodora now owns Win11 on their side directly. Central wave officially moved from 9 Mar to 23 Mar, BranchOne vendor patch expected 16 Mar.

Margot Delacroix starts as Lucerne's COO today. Draft a short intro email from me: who we are to Lucerne (digital platform retainer, royalties migration, metadata POC), and offer 30 min in her first few weeks. Warm but not salesy.

Ottilie came back on the pricing: wants the 2-yr at +2% and observability at $50k instead of $65k. A 2-yr term means it goes to their board on 10 Mar, so Bianca needs final numbers by Thu. Signature by 24 Mar. Duncan backs us but won't overrule finance.
remind me what floor we agreed in the internal Proseware pricing review, and under what condition?

Wilhelmina ok'd the 20 Apr cutover but wants a parallel run of the old system for the spring statements as a fallback. That's ~6 extra days from us ($8.4k) and she wants it absorbed inside the $16.8k CR. Pushing back.

Investment committee approved the Woodgrove MDR in principle! But Augustin Valcourt wants a 2-yr term instead of 3 and a break clause after 12 months. Harriet wants it signed by end of March. Our deal desk says 2-yr is $299k/yr, negotiating.
Got sign-off on our side for Proseware: 2-yr at +2% ($418.2k/yr) with observability at $56k, so $474.2k/yr total. Meets Ottilie partway on observability. That's my final position.

Lucerne metadata POC interim: 1,400 of 2,000 titles tagged, 81% accuracy vs the editors' 200-title benchmark. BISAC codes doing better than keywords. Felix pleased but wants to see 85% before he takes it to Margot.
what's still open on Woodgrove before end of March? deadlines and owners pls

Lucerne weekly cutover report #3 for Wilhelmina + Nkechi: data cleanup amber (1,900 of the 3,100 manual reviews done), cutover 20 Apr agreed, parallel run for the statements still being negotiated, statements 30 Apr amber, environments green.

Draft the revised offer to Ottilie Marchbank (cc Bianca): 2-yr at +2% = $418.2k/yr, observability at $56k (between her $50k and our $65k), total $474.2k/yr, and the $18k pilot fee credited in month 1. Sending tonight so it's there for her 7am read.

Woodgrove MDR closed on Fri: Augustin Valcourt's sign-off came through Harriet's office at $292k/yr (deal desk came down from $299k), 2-yr, break after 12 months with 90 days notice, $24k onboarding. Contract is with Josh's team for vendor risk review, 10 working days. Josh also confirmed our due diligence questionnaire is closed.

Woodgrove Feb service desk numbers: FCR 71.2% (up from 68%), CSAT 4.3, 17,900 tickets. Knowledge push is working. Teodora asked us to keep the 2 extra L2 engineers 4 more weeks and offered to pay half.

Lucerne: Margot Delacroix wants a review of every vendor contract over $100k by end of April. That includes our $312k retainer renewing 1 May. And Felix told me the Shopify agency has been asked for a formal quote. Retainer is at real risk.
Wilhelmina replied Fri: she'll pay $4.2k for the parallel run, half of the $8.4k, we absorb the rest. Taking it. Cutover stays 20 Apr.

Proseware pilot week 3 numbers posted in #proseware-ops: noise down 61%, MTTR 28 min (-40% vs 47). Both criteria met with 2+ weeks to go. Ottilie said yes in principle to the $474.2k/yr this morning, board is tomorrow. Yusuf wants the data retention settings in writing before full rollout.

prep for Thursday's 2pm Woodgrove renewal kickoff with Harriet and Teodora. Service desk is $1.15M, renews 30 Jun. FCR 71.2% now, the 26 Feb outage, MDR just closed at $292k. What's our position and what are they going to ask for?

prep me for my first meeting with Margot Delacroix on Thu 12 Mar at 11. She's reviewing vendors over $100k, our retainer renews 1 May, Felix getting a Shopify agency quote, royalties cutover 20 Apr, POC at 81%. What's my story and what do I not say?
Proseware board approved the 2-yr CloudOps renewal today, $474.2k/yr. Paperwork by 24 Mar, and Bianca wants it as an amendment to the existing MSA, not a new contract.

draft a thank-you and next steps email to Duncan and Raf: board approved, MSA amendment by 24 Mar, full observability rollout planning from 26 Mar once the pilot ends on the 25th, and Yusuf's retention settings doc from us by Fri.
quick one before I see Margot at 11 - what's the Lucerne retainer worth a year and when exactly does it renew?

Margot meeting went ok, she's sharp. Wants a retainer proposal with 2 options by 27 Mar: like-for-like at $312k and a reduced run-only option. Felix was noncommittal. Wilhelmina wants the same doc, in Word obviously.

Woodgrove renewal kickoff: Harriet wants a 3-yr renewal with a 4% reduction in return for the term, and FCR 74% written into the new SLA. Agreed the 2 extra L2s stay 4 more weeks, cost split 50/50. Exit plan to Josh still due 31 Mar. Next session 26 Mar.

weekly cutover report #4 for Wilhelmina + Nkechi: data cleanup green (all 11,000 records clean as of yesterday), parallel run agreed at $4.2k, cutover 20 Apr green, statements 30 Apr amber moving to green. Thank Nkechi properly, she carried this.

Draft a note to Augustin Valcourt confirming the MDR terms, to go via Harriet's office as usual: $292k/yr, 2-yr, break after 12 months on 90 days notice, $24k onboarding, service start 1 Aug for the overlap. Also flag that service desk renewal talks have started ahead of 30 Jun.
summarise where Proseware stands so I can paste it into my forecast notes: deal value and term, key dates, the pilot, open risks, and who's who now after Duncan's promotion.
